title: Introduce export lineage tokens and TTL-based dedupe to eliminate transient duplicate invoice lines
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Intermittent retry storms and race windows in the hourly export pipeline occasionally create pseudo-duplicate invoice lines in downstream Stripe/NetSuite exports. These duplicates are typically transient (same semantic usage but different export IDs or timestamps) and cause manual reconciliation work and customer confusion. Existing mitigations (watermarking and deterministic merge) have reduced frequency but do not prevent duplicates that emerge from out-of-order leader restarts, partial backfills, or multi-worker write races.

Goal: Add end-to-end lineage tokens to usage records produced by the ingestion tier and carry that token through aggregation and export. Use a TTL-based dedupe table in the export reconciler to detect semantically-equivalent lines within a configurable time window (default 48 hours). Ensure dedupe checks are idempotent and crash-recovery safe. Provide an opt-in dry-run mode for first rollout and strong observability (metrics and export-level flags) to measure false positives/negatives before enforcement.

Why unique: Instead of only relying on export fingerprints (hash of timestamp/account/amount), this change introduces a generated lineage token at produce-time and pairs it with a parity-key that tolerates acceptable timestamp discretization. The TTL-dedupe approach reduces the need for aggressive backfill suppression and supports safe local retries and replays from the ingestion queue.
technical_design: Generate a UUIDv7 lineage_token for each raw-metering record at producer (ingestion) and attach to event envelope.

Propagate lineage_token through aggregation pipeline; when merging usage windows, keep canonical lineage_token list (up to N tokens) and store parity_key = sha256(account_id + sku + bucket_start_minute).
Export line payload will include lineage_tokens[] and parity_key; reconciler will compute export_fingerprint = sha256(parity_key + quantity + price_cents + proration_bucket_id).

Introduce an export_dedupe table (primary key: export_fingerprint) with columns: first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts, exported_line_id, enforcement_state (dry-run|enforced), and ttl indexed by first_seen_ts. TTL default 48h, configurable per-customer via feature-flag.

Dedupe logic: on candidate export line, check export_dedupe for matching fingerprint within TTL. If found and enforcement_state==enforced, skip duplicate write and emit metric 'export.dedupe.skipped'. If dry-run, write metric 'export.dedupe.detected' but still allow export to proceed.
Leader election adjustment: reconciler leader checkpoints must persist the last applied dedupe watermark to avoid gap-induced false dedupe on leader failover.

Backfill/repair runner: use lineage_tokens to join historical rows and apply conservative merging rules (sum quantities when lineage sets disjoint), and produce a 'repair delta' PR to accounting with human approval for high-impact changes.
Edge cases: support multi-currency exports by including currency_code in parity_key; handle sub-minute metering by normalizing bucket_start to N-second epoch as customer config.
Observability: add histograms for dedupe_lookup_latency, counters for dedupe_hits/dedupe_misses/false_positive_alerts, and an export_anomaly dashboard showing top accounts by dedupe rate.
Backward compatibility: if lineage_token not present (old events), fall back to existing fingerprinting logic and mark entry as legacy in export_dedupe table.
acceptance_criteria: Lineage token is generated and persisted on newly ingested meter events in staging and prod-shadow pipelines.
Export reconciler in dry-run mode flags >95% of expected duplicates (based on historical sample) without skipping actual writes.
When enforcement is toggled on for a limited customer subset, exported duplicates reduce by >=90% for that cohort over a 7-day window without loss of legitimate distinct lines.
No customer invoices are altered silently during dry-run phase; any automated repair runs require explicit review for high-delta (> $500) invoice deltas.
Metrics and dashboards are created and populating within 24 hours of staging rollout; alerts for dedupe spike (>=5x baseline) notify SRE and Billing owners.
Automated unit and integration tests cover dedupe table writes, TTL expiry, leader failover replay, and legacy fallback behavior.
tasks: Spike: implement minimal lineage_token propagation in ingestion (2d) - @mateo
Schema: create export_dedupe table and migration with TTL index (1d) - @backend-db
Reconciler: add dry-run dedupe check and metric emission (3d) - @mateo
Reconciler: enforcement path and skip-write branch with audit logging (2d) - @mateo
Observability: Grafana dashboard + alerts and SLI targets (1d) - @observability
QA: run 72h shadow exports against staging dataset and compare to baseline for false positives (2d) - @qa
Rollout: feature-flagged gradual enablement and canary on subset customers (1d) - @infra
Backfill harness: conservative repair runner and human approval flow (3d) - @billing-eng
qa_plan: Create synthetic dataset containing known duplicate scenarios (retries, out-of-order timestamps, leader restart) and validate dedupe detection in dry-run.
Compare staging exports (dry-run) against prod-baseline for sample customers across 72h; compute precision/recall of detection.
Run integration with Stripe sandbox and a NetSuite test tenant to ensure skipped writes do not break export contract and mapping identifiers remain stable.
Simulate leader failover during active export window and validate reconcile checkpointing does not lead to lost or extra dedupe decisions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging shadow): enable lineage token generation and reconciler dry-run for all staging exports; validate metrics (1 week).
Phase 1 (canary prod dry-run): enable dry-run mode for 5% of customers selected by low-complexity SKU distribution; monitor false-positive rate and infra cost (1 week).
Phase 2 (targeted enforcement): flip enforcement on for low-risk cohort (non-enterprise customers) and run 7-day monitoring; keep emergency kill-switch via FF (48h rollback window).
Phase 3 (global enforcement): widen enforcement to all customers after observed stability and thresholds met; schedule post-rollout audit and run repair harness for any residual anomalies.
comments: 2025-03-12 Aisha Kapoor: Triage - customer ops reported 3 manual tickets this week tied to duplicate invoice lines after a partial backfill. Decided to pursue lineage-token approach after quick spike showed fingerprints alone were brittle.

2025-03-14 Mateo Alvarez: Spike notes - generating UUIDv7 adds monotonicity helpful for ordering; storing token list on aggregated rows increases row size, limiting to 8 tokens per row seems safe based on 99th percentile of upstream event fan-in.
2025-03-16 Design review with Billing PM (Sana): agreed on conservative enforcement and human-in-the-loop for repair changes > $500; added requirement to include currency in parity_key.
2025-03-18 Engineering review: DB migration reviewed by @backend-db, recommended TTL index partitioning by month to avoid hot partitions; adjusted migration plan accordingly.

2025-03-20 Mateo Alvarez: Implementation update - ingestion change is deployed to staging shadow; reconciler dry-run implemented behind FF and metrics are appearing. Next: run 72h shadow and analyze results.
